This appeal is filed by the claimants challenging the judgment and award dated 05.08.2010, passed in MVC No.2112/1997, by the I Addl. Senior Civil Judge and MACT, Belagavi, seeking enhancement of compensation as well as seeking modification of liability to pay compensation.

3. Heard the arguments and perused the records.
NC: 2023:KHC-D:14675 4.

In the present case the tribunal while determining the compensation has fastened liability on respondent No.1 owner of the tempo on the reason that the tempo was being transported and its body was not built; in the said tempo in the cabin the deceased was travelling and died in the accident.
Ex.R.1 is the insurance policy which is Motor Trade Transit Policy.
Admittedly the body of tempo was not built.
It was being transported for building its body.
In the cabin the deceased was travelling.
Admittedly the policy is not issued under section 147 of the M.V.Act, but Ex.R.1 insurance policy is Motor Trade Transit Policy (MTTP).
As per this MTTP policy only driver alone is covered.

This nature of policy is a purely contractual in nature between respondents No.1 and 2 so as to cover Annappa Prabhu Kamate vs The Manager on 14 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/92683990/

sentences.text: The nature and character of Ex.R.1 insurance policy is perused and is not issued as per section 147 of the M.V.Act so as to compulsorily cover the persons enumerated under section 147 of the M.V.Act.
Therefore under these type of pure contractual policy as Motor Trade Transit Policy, except the NC: 2023:KHC-D:14675 driver, no other persons risk is covered.
The deceased was not driver, but occupant in the cabin, which is not permissible as per law and also as per Ex.R.1 MTTP policy.
Therefore, the tribunal has rightly exonerated the insurance company to indemnify the owner and to pay compensation.
Therefore, respondent No.1 owner alone is responsible for payment of compensation on account of death of deceased.
5. The learned counsel for appellant submitted an order of pay and recovery can be made.
An order of pay and recovery can be made as per sub-section (1) of section 147 of the M.V.Act only where the insurance policy is issued as per section 147 of the M.V.Act.

Where the insurance policy is statutory policy compulsorily coverable all the persons enumerated in the said section and if there is any violation of conditions of policy, then an order of pay and recovery can be made.
But in the present case the policy issued is not a statutory policy compulsorily to be issued as per section 147 of the M.V.Act.
Ex.R.1 policy NC: 2023:KHC-D:14675 is a purely contractual policy between the owner and insurer nomenclatured as Motor Trade Transit Policy covering the risk of driver alone but not to others.
Therefore the order of pay and recovery cannot be made.

Therefore, in the absence of proof of income, the notional income would be Rs.3,000/- per month as recognized by the Karnataka State Legal Service Authority.
The claimants are husband and four children.

Therefore 1/4th of the income is to be deducted towards personal and living NC:
2023:KHC-D:14675 expenses.

Considering the age of the claimant, the appropriate applicable multiplier is 17.
8.

Considering the age of the deceased at the time of accident, in view of the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in case of National Insurance Company Limited vs. Pranay Sethi and others, reported in (2017) 16 Supreme Court Cases 680, 40% of the income is to be added towards loss of future prospects in life.
